correctness.rationale: For each s_v>=2, two initially white private-clique vertices can never be forced (twin unique-neighbor obstruction). If root initially blue or its private clique all blue, local forces activate root and entire clique. Otherwise root and exactly one private vertex white, so no private force can activate root; it must be forced through a base edge. Hence effective B(S) is ZF of G iff S is ZF of H. For v in B, local generating factor x^s_v(x+s_v+1); for v outside B, s_v x^(s_v-1). Product/sum yields exact polynomial, coefficient formula, minimum cardinality and minimum-set multiplicities. For uniform s polynomial composition is injective. Independent direct exhaustive brute-force checks over 74 decorated small graphs tested 111768 initial sets, no mismatch. Counterexample when s=1 validates boundary.

value.rationale: PASS: an exact full zero-forcing polynomial transfer for arbitrary bases and heterogeneous clique decorations is a natural structural counting theorem. It provides every coefficient, minimum set count and equivalence reflection, substantially beyond the previously known scalar Z(G) identity and useful for constructing graph families with controlled forcing distributions.
